findings.trigger: displayName now resolves through entriesByKey, and isStated now normalises through it. That index includes looseAliases, which name a related skill, not the same one. Probe at head: displayName('SwiftUI')=Swift, displayName('AngularJS')=Angular, displayName('Shell scripting')=Bash. keywordsStatedIn(req('Shell scripting'), 'Wrote shell scripting tools') returns [Bash]. AddUserStatedFactUseCase then writes 'Bash' to profile.skills and userStatedSkills, so a skill the user never typed can reach the exported skills section. keywordsStatedIn(req('SwiftUI'), 'Wrote Swift code') returns [Swift], so the SwiftUI requirement counts as covered (keywordOf collapses both to 'swift'). ScreenForKeywords shows the JD's 'SwiftUI' as 'Swift' and merges AngularJS with Angular. After #308 copies the file, a YES to an 'AngularJS' or 'Shell scripting' requirement puts 'Angular' or 'Bash' in the TailorResumeUseCase:150 allowlist. Base c291999f already gave [Bash] for the canonical keyword 'bash' against 'shell scripting'. This delta widens that to JD keywords that are loose aliases. Fix: resolve displayName and isStated only through display plus strict aliases. Leave a looseAliases keyword on the stem path, where 'Built SwiftUI apps' confirms 'SwiftUI' verbatim. TokenSubset already filters loose surfaces the same way via isLooseSurface.

findings.trigger: The Go and Express lexicon entries have matchesCanonical=false and no bare exactForm. canonicalsIn therefore never yields them for bare 'Go' or 'Express'. Now that isStated normalises every lexicon keyword, keywordsStatedIn(req('Go'), 'Built services in Go') returns []. The same holds for 'Express' vs 'Built APIs with Express', and isNamedSkillKeyword(req('Go'), 'Go') with text 'Experience with Go' is false. On c291999f the display-cased 'Go' that the prod backend emits was confirmed by stem, but that also over-matched 'go-to-market'. The new behaviour is safe, with no truth risk, but a 'Go' requirement can now be confirmed only by 'golang'. After #308 copies the file, a blank-detail YES_REGULARLY for SKILL 'Go' adds no answer keyword, because #308's own isNamedSkillKeyword returned true for any SKILL/TOOL. 'Go' therefore drops out of the skills allowlist. Fix: add a guarded case-sensitive exactForm 'Go' (block a following '-') and 'Express' to TechLexicon, or record the limit in D42 and test the expected [] for 'Built services in Go'.
